Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Private VPC Discovery Recap — FinHealth regulated workloads

Hi Jane / Luke —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call + proposed next steps so we’re all aligned. Please reply if I missed anything.

1) Primary pain points
- Regulated workloads with strict data residency and audit requirements (HIPAA + regional controls).
- Customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) requirement for encryption at rest and in-transit key control.
- Network constraints: private VPC connectivity only, strict egress rules, explicit allowlists (no public internet for inference).
- Potential need for air-gapped or on-prem package for certain environments.

2) Current stack (what you described)
- Core ML infra: on-prem OpenShift cluster for sensitive workloads, plus Azure for non-sensitive batch processing.
- Identity & access: Active Directory + SAML; IT owns key lifecycle and rotation.
- Existing procurement: long security review cycles; required SOC2 and penetration testing evidence.

3) Success criteria (what would make this a win for FinHealth)
- Private deployment option (VPC or on-prem) that meets NetSec policies and does not require traffic to traverse public internet.
- Ability to bring-your-own-keys (BYOK) and integrate with HSM/KMS for key custody.
- Audit logs and retention options compatible with your compliance requirements.
- Predictable latency and throughput for production workloads and an upgrade path for burst capacity.

4) Constraints / unknowns we flagged
- Whether the air-gapped on-prem package will be required for Phase 1 or can be scoped for Phase 2.
- Exact HSM vendor and integration constraints (Thales, Azure Key Vault Managed HSM, etc.).
- Network architecture details (egress vs. internal-only requests to model runtime) — need network diagrams from your infra team.

5) Next steps
- Marissa: share our Private/VPC checklist and a draft SOW for scope and commercial discussion. (attached)
- Luke / IT: share network diagram and HSM/KMS vendor details.
- Dylan: schedule a technical deep-dive / demo with your infra and security teams — proposed window next week.
- Align on timelines and procurement process (expected security review lead times).

Attachments: finhealth-sow.pdf (draft SOW), redwood-private-vpc-checklist.xlsx

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
https://redwoodinference.com
From: Luke Carter <luke.carter@finhealth.com>

Cc: Jane Doe <jane.doe@finhealth.com>, IT Security <it-security@finhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 17:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private VPC Discovery Recap — FinHealth regulated workloads

Thanks Marissa — useful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- BYOK: we require HSM-backed keys and we use Azure Key Vault Managed HSM for cloud. For on-prem sensitive environments we may require Thales HSM integration or similar. Can you confirm supported HSM integrations and whether Redwood will accept customer-managed keys?

- Egress: for Phase 1 we need the runtime to have no outbound traffic to the public internet; any necessary model downloads or updates must go through our approved mirrors or be staged by our infra team. Is an air-gapped deployment option documented?

- Audit logs: we need audit logs with immutable retention for 2 years and the ability to export to our SIEM.

I’ve looped in our IT Security alias to provide network diagrams and the procurement timeline.

Luke
VP Engineering, FinHealth
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Luke Carter <luke.carter@finhealth.com>, Jane Doe <jane.doe@finhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private VPC Discovery Recap — FinHealth regulated workloads

Appreciate the details, Luke. Short answers: 
- HSM/KMS: Redwood Private supports BYOK patterns and integrations with common cloud KMS providers; for on-prem Thales/HSM we support customer-managed HSM via PKCS#11 or appliance integrations — will validate with engineering and provide a short compatibility matrix.
- Air-gap: we have a documented on-prem package and an air-gapped install checklist. The package requires a one-time transfer of model artifacts and our installer is designed to run without outbound internet after staging.
- Audit logs: runtime and control-plane logs can be exported to S3-compatible stores or pushed to your SIEM via our secure connector; retention policies are configurable.

Next practical step: can we schedule a technical deep-dive with your infra/security team Wednesday or Thursday next week (PST)? I can bring our product engineer (Aditya) to answer HSM and network questions.

Action items I’ll do after this thread: share the compatibility matrix and the air-gap install doc.

Thanks,
Dylan
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
